text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak said yesterday there is no alternative to peace, because it is a stability valve for the region and the peace process must be pursued, whether the states in the region want to or not. He said the alternative to peace is not war, but violence and terrorism, which counterforces would practise without distinguishing between one state and another. He said peace would only come about through the Palestinians obtaining their rights, the restoration of the Golan Heights to Syria and Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif, briefing journalists after Mubarak's meeting with the secretariat of the Union of Arab Journalists and commenting on the Boutros-Ghali affair, said: "It seems the international order practises democracy of a special kind."

- The cabinet said that at the Middle East economic conference agreements were signed on giant projects worth a total of $4.8 billion and negotations are continuing between Egyptian, Arab and foreign partners on projects worth a further $6.8 billion -- in the iron, petrochemical, cement and newsprint industries. Safwat el-Sherif said the cabinet decided to organise an annual economic forum in Egypt.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said that at its meeting on December 2 the group of economic ministers would look at new incentives for investment in Egypt, including tax and customs privileges to attract investment to southern Egypt, Sinai and the Western Desert.

- Mubarak told the Union of Arab Journalists that the future of Egypt was in a new demographic map and that the Peace Canal and the Sheikh Zaid canals are projects to take Egypt to the horizons of the next century.

- Egypt's ambassador to Washington, Ahmed Maher, reported to Mubarak on the situation in the United States after the U.S. elections. He told Mubarak that the United States appreciated the evolution in the Egyptian economy.

- Life has returned to normal in the Red Sea resort of Hurghada after the floods ended. The telephones and electricity supply in the province have been restored. Qena was the province worst hit this year and in some places there were two metres (seven feet) of water.
- Mubarak warned of violence and terrorism if the peace process does not succeed.
- The cabinet agreed to let civil servants take unpaid leave indefinitely, except in departments covered by special laws, like schools and Azhar institutes.
- Thirteen people have been killed in the floods in the south and in south Sinai and nine have been hospitalised with injuries. In Assiut five people were electrocuted.
